title: Join realization and its cubical boundary-extension data
statement:
Use simplicial sets, standard simplices, boundaries and enriched mapping sets of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the subset-poset coherent realization $\mathfrak C$ of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching]. For small simplicial sets $X,Y$, let $\star$ be the ordered join (an $r$-simplex is a pure simplex of either factor or a pair of simplices whose dimensions sum to $r-1$, with the $X$ block first). The full subcategories of $\mathfrak C[X\star Y]$ on the two blocks are $\mathfrak C[X]$ and $\mathfrak C[Y]$. There are no maps from the second block to the first. For vertices $x$ of $X$ and $y$ of $Y$ there is a natural simplicial isomorphism
$$\mathfrak C[X\star Y](x,y)\cong\mathfrak C[X\star\Delta^0](x,v)\times\mathfrak C[\Delta^0\star Y](b,y),$$
where $v$ is the new last vertex and $b$ the new first vertex. The actions of the two full subcategories are the respective actions on these factors; this description is natural in maps of $X,Y$. In particular $\mathfrak C[\Delta^0\star Y]$ has boundary $A=\mathfrak C[Y]$, one new vertex $b$ with identity endomorphism simplicial set $\Delta^0$, no maps from $A$ to $b$, and outgoing weight $W_Y(a)=\mathfrak C[\Delta^0\star Y](b,a)$. Its enriched functors into a simplicial category $\mathcal D$, with fixed boundary functor $F:A\to\mathcal D$ and fixed value $L$ at $b$, correspond to enriched natural maps $W_Y\to\mathcal D(L,F(-))$.

More precisely, let $n\ge1$ and let $H:\mathfrak C[\partial\Delta^n\star Y]\to\mathcal D$ be any enriched functor, with $F=H|_A$ and $z_i=H(i)$ for $0\le i\le n$. Here $\mathcal D$ need not be locally Kan. Let $\lambda_n:W_Y\to\mathcal D(z_n,F(-))$ be the cone at the last vertex of $\partial\Delta^n$. Put
$$M=\mathcal D(z_0,z_n),\quad T=\underline{\operatorname{Nat}}(W_Y,\mathcal D(z_0,F(-))),\quad u:M\to T,\qquad u(f)=f^*\lambda_n,$$
where $\underline{\operatorname{Nat}}(P,Q)_r$ is the set of enriched natural maps $P\times\Delta^r\to Q$, and $f^*\lambda_n$ means composition with $f$ in its source variable. Define $Q=(\Delta^1)^{n-1}$, with $Q=\Delta^0$ for $n=1$, and $\partial Q$ as the union of all coordinate endpoint faces (empty for $n=1$). Put $V=(\partial Q\times\Delta^1)\cup(Q\times\{0\})$. Order the coordinates of $Q$ by the vertices $1,\ldots,n-1$. The restriction of $H$ to $\mathfrak C[\partial\Delta^n](0,n)\cong\partial Q$ defines $\alpha:\partial Q\to M$. Let $v$ denote the last vertex adjoined to $\partial\Delta^n$. The characteristic-function coordinates of $\mathfrak C[\partial\Delta^n\star\Delta^0](0,v)\cong V$ are ordered by $1,\ldots,n$, with the final $\Delta^1$ recording membership of $n$. For each vertex $y$ of $Y$, the cross-mapping formula identifies $\mathfrak C[\partial\Delta^n\star Y](0,y)$ with $V\times W_Y(y)$. The maps on these mapping sets supplied by $H$, transposed and assembled by enriched naturality in $y$, define $\beta:V\to T$. Composition through the vertex $n$ gives $\beta|_{\partial Q\times\{1\}}=u\alpha$. Extensions of $H$ to $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n\star Y]$ correspond bijectively to pairs
$$a:Q\to M,\qquad c:Q\times\Delta^1\to T$$
satisfying $a|_{\partial Q}=\alpha$, $c|_V=\beta$, and $c|_{Q\times\{1\}}=ua$. This correspondence fixes all the already prescribed data, including the boundary diagram and every cone at a boundary vertex.

source.place: Riehl–Verity, Theorem 5.3.19 and Remark 5.3.21 (printed pp. 41–42), Proposition 6.1.8 and its cubical presentation (printed pp. 44–45); Definition 5.2.8 and Corollary 5.2.4 for the collage. Read online; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this enriched realization calculation.

proof.text: Use the unique bead words of [lem-coef-coherent-realization-bead-normal-form]. A nondegenerate mixed simplex of $X\star Y$ is uniquely $\sigma\star\tau$, where $\sigma$ and $\tau$ are nondegenerate simplices of the two factors: a simplicial degeneracy repeats adjacent ordinal positions, necessarily within one block; equality of vertex values alone does not imply degeneracy. A bead therefore goes within one block or crosses once from X to Y; none goes backwards. A word between two X vertices, or between two Y vertices, consists entirely of beads in that block. The subcomplex-detection clause proves that the two realizations are full and the reverse mapping sets are empty. Every cross word consists of a pure X word, exactly one mixed bead, and a pure Y word.

source.place: §5.1 Proposition 5.1.12 applied to the ordered join; §5.3 Remark 5.3.21, block structure.

proof.text: The two collapse maps $X\star Y\to X\star\Delta^0$ and $X\star Y\to\Delta^0\star Y$ define the cross-mapping map in the statement. On a mixed bead with simplex $\sigma\star\tau$ and flag $T_\bullet$, the first collapse retains $T_a\cap X$ and adds the last vertex v; the second retains $T_a\cap Y$ and adds the first vertex b. Both resulting flags begin with their two endpoints and finish with the full vertex set, so they are beads. Conversely, a bead ending at v and one starting at b have underlying simplices $\sigma\star v$ and $b\star\tau$. Remove v and b from their flags and take their ordered union at each index a. This gives the unique bead on $\sigma\star\tau$ projecting to that pair; weak flags allow repetitions in either factor. A word ending at v has a unique pure X prefix and a final mixed bead, since v has only its identity endomorphism. A word starting at b has an initial mixed bead and a pure Y suffix. Joining their two mixed beads therefore gives the unique inverse on cross words. This proves bijectivity in every simplicial degree, including nondegenerate simplices of X or Y whose endpoint vertices coincide.

source.place: Theorem 5.3.19 and Remark 5.3.21; direct proof using the general bead normal form, rather than assuming connected-colimit preservation.

proof.text: The forward map in Step 2 is induced by actual simplicial collapse maps, so its degreewise inverse is a simplicial inverse. Pre- and postcomposition append beads only in the corresponding pure block, proving the asserted two actions. The collapse squares commute for all maps of X and Y; their inverses are therefore natural too, even when a map makes a bead simplex degenerate. For $X=\Delta^0$ the first block is a single object with endomorphism $\Delta^0$. Hence the whole category has exactly the stated collage hom-objects. Assigning F and L leaves maps $W_Y(a)\to\mathcal D(L,F(a))$ to specify. The only nonidentity composition equations left are $\lambda_{a'}(g w)=F(g)\lambda_a(w)$; these are exactly enriched naturality. Restriction and this assignment are inverse, proving the collage assertion.

source.place: Remark 5.3.21; Definition 5.2.2 and Corollary 5.2.4, with the enriched functor equations written explicitly.

proof.text: In $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n](0,n)$ a degree-r simplex is a flag $S_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq S_r$ of endpoint-containing subsets of $[n]$, by [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching]. Its interior characteristic coordinates are the cube Q. Split it at the vertices of $S_0$ into its unique beads. The subcomplex criterion says it is in $\mathfrak C[\partial\Delta^n]$ precisely when every bead has proper support. If an interior vertex is in $S_0$, there are at least two beads, each on a proper face. If none is in $S_0$, there is one bead, and its support is proper exactly when an interior vertex is absent from $S_r$. Thus membership means some coordinate is constantly 1 or constantly 0, exactly $\partial Q$. For $n=1$ there are no interior coordinates and no such flags, so this is the empty boundary of $Q=\Delta^0$.

source.place: Example 5.1.10(i), boundary cube, derived using the cited bead normal form.

proof.text: Write $v=n+1$ and $K=\partial\Delta^n\star\{v\}\subset\Delta^{n+1}$. The missing nondegenerate simplices are exactly $[0,n]$ and $[0,n+1]$, with endpoints $(0,n)$ and $(0,v)$. The bead criterion therefore makes every other mapping set unchanged. For a flag from 0 to v, if an index j with $1\leq j<n$ is constantly absent, its support is contained in an allowed face; if j is constantly present, splitting there gives two proper supports, both in K. If there is no such j, all coordinates $1,\ldots,n-1$ begin at 0 and end at 1. When coordinate n is constantly 0, the support omits n and lies in K. When coordinate n starts at 0 and ends at 1, the single bead has forbidden full support. When coordinate n is constantly 1, the factor from 0 to n is the forbidden bead on $[0,n]$. These cases exhaust the flags, so the allowed set is $V=(\partial Q\times\Delta^1)\cup(Q\times\{0\})$. In the full category composition through n is insertion of that vertex into every subset, exactly the inclusion $Q\times\{1\}\hookrightarrow Q\times\Delta^1$.

source.place: Example 5.1.10(ii); Proposition 6.1.8 and the explicit cube display at the end of printed p.45.

proof.text: Apply the natural join factorization of Steps 1–3 to X equal to $\partial\Delta^n$ and to $\Delta^n$. The first-cone factor at 0 changes from V to $Q\times\Delta^1$, while the second factor is always $W_Y(y)$. H supplies maps $V\times W_Y(y)\to\mathcal D(z_0,F(y))$ satisfying the Y-action equations. Transposition in each simplicial degree identifies these maps with $\beta:V\to T$: an r-simplex of T is, by its definition, a natural family $W_Y(y)\times\Delta^r\to\mathcal D(z_0,F(y))$. Similarly restriction on the 0-to-n mapping set gives $\alpha:\partial Q\to M$. Composition through n, identified in Step 5 with the last coordinate 1, is $\lambda_n(w)\circ\alpha(q)$ for every w. Therefore the exact boundary equation is $\beta|_{\partial Q\times\{1\}}=u\alpha$, with u as in the statement.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.8, equations (6.1.10) and its composition square, printed pp.44–45.

proof.text: Any extension restricts to a on $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n](0,n)=Q$ and to c on the first-cone factor $Q\times\Delta^1$, transposed over $W_Y$. Agreement with H gives $a|_{\partial Q}=\alpha$ and $c|_V=\beta$; composition through n gives $c|_{Q\times\{1\}}=ua$. Conversely use such a and c on the two changed types of mapping sets, and retain H everywhere else. There are no incoming nonidentity maps to vertex 0. A composition from 0 through j, $0<j<n$, lies on coordinate j constantly 1 and hence on $\partial Q$ or V, so its equation already holds for H. Composition from 0 through n and then into Y is exactly the equation $c(q,1)(w)=\lambda_n(w)\circ a(q)$. Compositions entirely within Y, or postcomposing a changed cross map by a Y-map, hold because every simplex of c is enriched natural. These are all possible nonidentity composition types by the ordered block structure; identities are retained. Thus the pair defines an enriched functor extending H. This also proves uniqueness: all its hom-maps are now specified.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.8, proof and composition square, with every possible changed composition checked.

proof.text: Restriction recovers exactly the a and c used to construct the extension, while construction retains every hom-map of an original extension. Thus this is a bijection fixing the entire prescribed subcategory, in particular all boundary cones. If $n=1$, then $\partial Q=\varnothing$ and $V=\{0\}$; the data are an edge $a\in\mathcal D(z_0,z_1)_0$ and a simplicial path c from the first cone to its composite with the last cone, with no assumption that either mapping set is Kan. If $Y=\varnothing$, T is the one-point natural-transformation simplicial set on the empty category, and c is unique; the correspondence reduces to extension of the sole changed hom-object $\partial Q\hookrightarrow Q$. If one factor X or Y is empty, the general join assertion has only its pure block and no cross vertex pair. These cases require no nonemptiness or fibrancy hypotheses.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.8, terminal-base specialization; explicit n=1 and empty-factor checks.

lean.statement: theorem join_boundary_cubical_extension : ∃ (O : Objects.{u}) (C : Cross O), C.IsCanonical ∧ C.IsNatural ∧ C.BlocksAndActions ∧ Collage.{u, v} O ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, ∃ B : Cubes O m, ∀ (Y : SSet.{u}) (D : Type v) [EnrichedCategory SSet.{u} D] (H : EnrichedFunctor SSet (PinchedCube.rigidification.obj (join (SSet.boundary (m + 1)) Y)) D), ExtensionClauses C B Y D H
lean.note: Reuses the recorded simplex-colimit rigidification, ordered join and cube boundary. All coordinate witnesses are existential conclusions normalized on simplex units and collapse maps; no definition chooses data from the theorem. The target enrichment has independent object universe v and mapping universe u. Parameterized enriched natural families define the actual transformation simplicial set.
